issues.body: The prior finding is not fixed. `if any(entry[0][0] in FLOW_WORDS for entry in lists)` checks only the first token of each `;`/`&`-delimited list. The later `commands.extend(split_on(list_tokens, "&&"))` can therefore record probes after a flow-control command later in that same list. For example, with PyYAML proven in a separate RUN, `RUN true && exit 0 && jq --version` is accepted: splitting records `["jq", "--version"]`, but `exit 0` terminates the shell before jq and the build remains green. `exec true` provides the analogous bypass. The existing `deps-flow.Dockerfile` fixture uses `RUN set -eux; exit 0; jq --version`, where `exit` begins its semicolon-delimited list, so it passes without testing the vulnerable post-`&&` path.
issues.fix_hint: Reject a RUN when a flow-control word begins any command produced after splitting every and-or list at `&&`, before recording probes from that RUN. Add non-vacuous fixtures with the other dependency genuinely proven and `RUN true && exit 0 && jq --version`, plus the analogous `exec true` form, asserting rejection and that jq is named.
issues.title: Flow control after && still permits unreachable probes

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 major remains unchanged. Flow-control rejection still checks only the first command of each semicolon/ampersand-delimited list, before splitting that list at `&&`. Consequently, a later `exit` or `exec` can make an accepted probe unreachable while the RUN succeeds. The sole flow fixture still puts `exit` at the beginning of its list and does not exercise the reported post-`&&` bypass. Progress is stagnant.
